papers.title: A Dynamic Model of Microsleep and Vigilance Tradeoffs in Nesting Chinstrap Penguins.
papers.summary: Adapted a dynamic sleep-choice model to published sleep data from 14 nesting chinstrap penguins, reproducing short microsleep bouts (mean 2.774 s vs 3.91 s observed) and frequent sleep-wake transitions. The model underestimated total sleep time and overproduced very short episodes, implying minimal switching costs and rapid homeostatic adjustment.

papers.title: Invertebrate brains as diversified models for understanding sleep mechanisms and function.
papers.journal: Journal of comparative physiology. A, Neuroethology, sensory, neural, and behavioral physiology
papers.summary: Reviews sleep in insects, particularly Apis mellifera, and presents new automated video data on polyphasic antennal movement sleep patterns. It compares invertebrate and vertebrate sleep to highlight conserved and divergent features relevant to memory consolidation, energy regulation, and catastrophic forgetting in artificial neural networks.

papers.title: An EEMD-derived slow-wave activity metric improves association with obstructive sleep apnea severity beyond conventional N3 staging.
papers.summary: Applied ensemble empirical mode decomposition to sleep EEG from 823 SHHS participants to derive slow-wave activity-based slow-wave sleep metrics. EEMD-derived SWS showed stronger correlations with apnea-hypopnea index (up to -0.70 in high-risk groups) than conventional N3 staging (around -0.27 to -0.28).

papers.title: Chronotype-specific associations of sleep-wake schedule with behavioral, physiological, and psychological parameters.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: Compared early and late chronotypes under socially imposed versus self-selected 8-hour sleep schedules, measuring subjective states, sleep pressure via EEG, and motor and cognitive performance at 1.5 and 12.5 hours after awakening. Early chronotypes showed typical sleep pressure accumulation, late chronotypes were more affected by sleep timing, and cognitive peaks depended on chronotype and wake duration rather than clock time alone.

papers.title: Active Bed Microclimate Regulation Modulates Sleep Architecture, Autonomic, and Central Nervous System Activity during Sleep
papers.summary: Used a smart bed with six active temperature settings to test effects on sleep architecture, autonomic activity, and EEG in 18 adults across two overnight polysomnography sessions. Active cooling and heating increased slow-wave sleep odds (OR 1.21-3.65) and altered heart rate and cortical activity, suggesting nonlinear thermal effects and individualized temperature strategies.

papers.title: Investigating the influence of anti-seizure medications on aperiodic EEG activity.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: In a placebo-controlled study with 13 healthy males, lamotrigine reduced aperiodic offset and exponent during eyes-open resting EEG, while levetiracetam reduced only the exponent; both drugs also altered periodic activity, indicating that aperiodic EEG measures can characterize distinct pharmacological effects on cortical activity.

papers.title: HIPPOCAMPAL TAU RELATED SIGNAL INDEXES HYPEREXCITABILITY AND NREM SLEEP MEMORY DYSFUNCTION IN TEMPORAL LOBE EPILEPSY
papers.summary: In 25 patients with unilateral temporal lobe epilepsy, higher ipsilateral hippocampal 18F-MK6240 tau tracer uptake was associated with greater focal seizure burden, lower N2 sleep spindle rate, higher N3 slow-wave rate, and impaired memory performance. The findings suggest hippocampal tau signal as a candidate marker of circuit vulnerability linked to NREM sleep-memory dysfunction.

papers.title: Altered EEG patterns co-vary with specific improvements in mind health at summer camp
papers.summary: In 30 adolescents, a three-week device-free nature-rich summer camp was followed by steeper aperiodic EEG slopes, increased DFA scaling exponents, reduced entropy and Lempel-Ziv complexity, and decreased alpha and beta power. These convergent EEG changes co-varied with improved focus, sleep quality, reduced restlessness/hyperactivity, and overall mind health, with high specificity in precision analyses.

papers.title: NeuroStream: spectral-spatio-temporal deep learning for visual stimulus classification from EEG.
papers.summary: The paper introduces NeuroStream-SST, a spectral-spatio-temporal deep learning framework that transforms raw EEG into a video-like representation and achieves high accuracy in the high-gamma band on the EEGCVPR40 dataset, outperforming existing methods under identical protocols, while also showing that decoding performance depends on temporal correlations between labels and sessions.

papers.title: Mood rhythms and circadian medicine for mood disorders.
papers.summary: This review provides a comprehensive overview of brain regions, neurotransmitters, and hormones involved in mood and emotions, highlighting their rhythmic changes and the influence of the circadian clock on mood, with a focus on major depressive and bipolar disorders and the relationship between treatments and clock/physiological rhythm phasing.

papers.title: Forecasting the course of bipolar disorder using rest-activity rhythms: Protocol for a multi-study modelling project.
papers.summary: This protocol describes the Tipping Point project, a multi-study prospective modeling project that aims to develop an algorithm forecasting bipolar disorder relapse from 24-hour rest-activity rhythms measured by actigraphy, and to investigate sleep and circadian rhythm disruption mechanisms, including system instability as a predictor of relapse and recovery.

papers.title: Multidimensional welfare profiling of broiler leg health under probiotic or antimicrobial growth-promoter supplementation and environmental enrichment.
papers.summary: Developed a multidimensional welfare-response profiling framework to evaluate broiler leg health under probiotic or antimicrobial growth-promoter supplementation and environmental enrichment in a 3×2 factorial experiment with 1,440 male broilers. No significant effects of dietary additive, enrichment, or their interaction were detected on the global welfare-response index or most biological domains, though probiotic-supplemented groups showed global leg-health profiles within the range of zinc-bacitracin groups and treatment responses were primarily domain-specific.

papers.title: Differentially Private EEG Feature Anonymization: A Privacy-Utility Case Study in Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: The paper studies subject-level differential privacy for clinical EEG-derived feature representations using Gaussian and Laplace perturbations across client-side, server-side, and decentralized training scenarios. Results show that perturbation can be integrated into EEG workflows, but mechanism choice, privacy parameters, and sensitivity calibration strongly affect data utility, highlighting a privacy-utility trade-off in small and imbalanced clinical EEG datasets.

papers.title: Socioeconomic status, stress, and actigraphy-derived measures of sleep among middle-aged to older African American adults.
papers.summary: Examined whether day-level stress mediates the association between socioeconomic status (SES) and actigraphy-derived sleep duration and quality in 150 middle-aged to older African American adults over five days. Lower SES was associated with greater variability in total sleep time and wake after sleep onset but not with mean nightly sleep, and day-level stress did not mediate the SES-sleep associations.

papers.title: Melatonin and Artificial Light: Effects on Maternal and Fetal Health During Pregnancy.
papers.summary: Reviewed evidence on melatonin's role during pregnancy and the effects of artificial light at night (ALAN) on maternal-fetal health, synthesizing human and animal studies. Exposure to ALAN reduces melatonin production and is associated with adverse maternal-fetal outcomes, while animal studies demonstrate causal effects of melatonin disruption and protective effects of supplementation; evidence is insufficient to recommend melatonin supplementation, but circadian hygiene measures may be advised.

papers.title: Causal Effects of Gut Microbiota on Morning Chronotype, Insomnia and Sleep Duration: A Two-Sample Mendelian Randomization Study.
papers.journal: Journal of central nervous system disease
papers.summary: Conducted a two-sample Mendelian randomization analysis using genome-wide association data to infer causal effects of 196 gut microbiota taxa on morning chronotype, insomnia, and sleep duration. Identified specific taxa positively and negatively associated with sleep traits, including Bifidobacteriales/Bifidobacteriaceae/Bifidobacterium negatively with morning chronotype, Oscillibacter negatively with insomnia, and Lentisphaerae/Victivallaceae positively with sleep duration.

papers.title: Young minds in distress: Exploring the global rise in youth mental health diagnoses.
papers.summary: Reviewed global epidemiological trends in youth mental health diagnoses, integrating evidence on neurobiological vulnerability, environmental drivers, and intervention strategies. The review highlights substantial rises in youth depression, suicide mortality, and self-harm in high-income countries, identifies sleep disruption as a central transdiagnostic risk factor, and proposes a three-tiered intervention framework emphasizing digital regulation, social-emotional learning, sleep health monitoring, and integrated care.

papers.title: The association of sleep health with epigenetic aging in early adolescence: exploratory insights from the Health Outcomes and Measures of the Environment study.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: This exploratory study examined associations between accelerometry-based sleep characteristics and epigenetic aging in 138 adolescents from the HOME Study. Overall associations were imprecise, but higher sleep fragmentation was associated with elevated epigenetic age acceleration among males (Hannum β = 0.885, 95% CI: 0.132, 1.638; interaction p = .005) but not females.

papers.title: Exploring the bidirectional relationship between disorders of arousal and stress. An observational epidemiological study in a large population of university students.
papers.summary: A web-based survey of 1049 university students assessed the prevalence of disorders of arousal (DoA) and their association with psychological distress. Sleep terrors (aOR = 1.25, 95% CI 1.06-1.47) and confusional arousals (aOR = 1.19, 95% CI 1.07-1.33), but not sleepwalking, were significantly associated with higher perceived distress, supporting a bidirectional relationship between stress and DoA.

papers.title: Mediating role of sleep duration in the association between problematic media use and sleep disturbance in children with neurodevelopmental disabilities.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 205 caregivers of children with neurodevelopmental disabilities examined whether sleep duration mediates the association between problematic media use and sleep disturbance. Sleep duration partially mediated the relationship, accounting for 18.3% of the total effect, while problematic media use remained directly associated with sleep disturbance (B = 1.383, p = 0.016).

papers.title: Maternal Depressive Symptoms and Toddler Sleep: Moderating Effects of Sleep Parenting Practices.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional survey of 126 Taiwanese mothers of toddlers, higher maternal depressive symptoms were associated with more severe toddler sleep problems and longer sleep latency; co-sleeping moderated the maternal depression–toddler sleep problem association, which was significant only in the co-sleeping group. Sleep routine consistency showed no moderating effect.

papers.title: Deep learning-based susceptibility map-weighted imaging analysis of dorsal nigral hyperintensity as a surrogate for dopamine transporter positron emission tomography in patients with idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder.
papers.summary: This retrospective study evaluated a deep learning model applied to susceptibility map-weighted imaging (SMwI) for predicting dopamine transporter PET abnormalities in 74 patients with idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder. The model achieved 78% sensitivity, 66.7% specificity, and 73% accuracy, with bilateral SMwI abnormalities strongly correlating with DAT PET positivity (92.3%).

papers.title: Exploration and Analysis of Traditional Chinese Medicine Syndrome Differentiation of Insomnia Based on Millimeter-Wave Radar.
papers.summary: This review proposes a millimeter-wave radar-based framework for objective traditional Chinese medicine syndrome differentiation of insomnia, mapping five insomnia syndromes to 15 quantitative indicators across sleep architecture, autonomic nervous function, respiratory pattern, and body movement behavior. It presents a theoretical pathogenesis-physiology mapping model intended to support non-contact nocturnal monitoring and later clinical validation against polysomnography.

papers.title: Development and temporal validation of a postoperative nomogram based on clinical, surgical, histopathological, and semi-quantitative EEG features for predicting seizure-free survival in children after focal epilepsy surgery.
papers.summary: This single-center retrospective cohort study developed and temporally validated a postoperative nomogram using clinical, surgical, histopathological, and semi-quantitative EEG predictors to estimate 1- and 2-year seizure-free survival in 256 children after focal epilepsy surgery. Five predictors were retained, including longer epilepsy duration, absence of a definitive structural MRI lesion, histopathological diagnosis, subtotal resection, and high NREM interictal spike index (>38 spikes/h), with a temporal validation C-index of 0.79.

papers.title: TMS-EEG Correlate of Suicidal Ideation in Individuals with Depression: A Multi-Site Synthesis.
papers.summary: In a multi-site synthesis of cross-sectional TMS-EEG data from 299 adults with major depressive disorder and at least one ineffective antidepressant trial, more negative N100 peak amplitude in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex was associated with greater suicidal ideation severity (OR=1.52) independent of age, sex, depression severity, and site. No significant association was found between suicidal ideation and global mean field amplitude AUC.

papers.title: Bridging Temporal and Spatial Scales: Contemporary Advances in EEG-fMRI Integration With a Focus on Epilepsy.
papers.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation oncology
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent methodological, data acquisition, and analytical advances in EEG-fMRI integration for epilepsy, emphasizing its complementary temporal and spatial resolution for characterizing epileptogenic networks and potential use in presurgical evaluation. It also notes remaining technical, analytical, and translational challenges for broader clinical adoption.

papers.title: Association Between Sleep Duration and Depressive Symptoms Among U.S. Adults: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2021-2023.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional NHANES 2021–2023 analysis of 3,727 U.S. adults found that short sleep duration was associated with higher odds of clinically significant depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 ≥10), with the strongest association among those sleeping ≤5 hours (aOR 3.21, 95% CI 2.18–4.75) compared to 7–8 hours.

papers.title: Lactylation and N6-Methyladenosine RNA modification in neuropsychiatric sequelae after intracerebral hemorrhage: a hypothesis-generating metabolic-glial-circuit framework.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on lactylation and m6A RNA modification in neuropsychiatric sequelae after intracerebral hemorrhage, proposing a hypothesis-generating metabolic-glial-circuit framework that separates demonstrated acute ICH mechanisms (e.g., H3K18la-METTL3-LCN2) from proposed downstream links to depression, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and sleep disturbance, while noting that no study has yet shown causality for persistent neuropsychiatric outcomes.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning for depression symptom classification in NHANES: Performance in a curated high-confidence corpus and the full survey population.
papers.summary: This study evaluated interpretable machine learning models for classifying PHQ-9 depressive-symptom status (PHQ-9 ≥5) in 37,959 NHANES participants, finding that LightGBM achieved near-perfect performance in a curated balanced corpus but only moderate full-population discrimination (ROC-AUC 0.726) with poor calibration, largely driven by sleep variables such as self-reported trouble sleeping.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence at the Boundary of Spiritual Experience and Psychopathology: A Scoping Review of Evidence from Türkiye, the USA, the UK, Poland, South Korea, and Israel.
papers.summary: A scoping review of nine studies from six countries mapped how AI mediates, reinforces, detects, predicts, or interprets religious and spiritual experiences at the boundary with psychosis and dissociation. Conversational AI was reported as a catalyst, amplifier, co-author, or object of spiritually framed delusions, while NLP and machine-learning models showed preliminary potential for identifying psychotic episodes and predicting relapse.

papers.title: Systematic Literature Review on Public Health Impacts of Tourette Syndrome and Persistent Tic Disorders: General Health, Health Conditions, and Health Behaviors.
papers.journal: Journal of child and adolescent psychopharmacology
papers.summary: This systematic review of 84 studies found that individuals with Tourette syndrome or persistent tic disorders had higher prevalence of several poor health indicators and conditions—including lower health-related quality of life, overall poor health/disability, mortality, injuries, suicidal thoughts and behaviors, orthopedic and neurological disorders, sleep disorders, endocrine and immune-related disorders, and hearing/vision problems—while findings were inconsistent for gastrointestinal, circulatory, infection, and fever outcomes and did not differ for BMI or health behaviors.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights into di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate exposure in obstructive sleep apnea: network toxicology and in vitro validation.
papers.summary: Using NHANES data and network toxicology with in vitro validation in human bronchial epithelial cells, this study found that increased DEHP exposure was associated with higher all-cause mortality risk in OSA patients and that DEHP induced concentration-dependent changes in hub genes (AR, CASP3, PRKCA, CTSS, MMP9 up; BCL2 down) that were enhanced under chronic intermittent hypoxia.

papers.title: Consensus practice recommendations for management of sleep dysfunction in Parkinson disease.
authors: Other Non-motor Features Working Group of the Parkinson Study Group
papers.summary: A modified Delphi panel of 11 movement- and sleep-trained neurologists developed 114 consensus statements (100% agreement) covering screening, diagnosis, and treatment of sleep dysfunction in Parkinson disease, including insomnia, excessive daytime sleepiness, REM sleep behavior disorder, and other sleep disorders.

papers.title: Identifying JAK2 and ANXA5 as Key Genes Linking Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Oxidative Stress via Machine Learning and Multilayer Transcriptomic Integration With Functional Validation.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Integrating bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with machine learning, the study identified JAK2 (upregulated) and ANXA5 (downregulated) as key oxidative-stress-related genes in obstructive sleep apnea with high diagnostic accuracy (AUC > 0.85), validated by RT-qPCR and Western blotting, and implicated monocyte subtype remodeling and immune-inflammatory pathways.

papers.title: Application of the Omaha System-Based Nursing Model in the Perioperative Care of Patients Undergoing Pancreaticoduodenectomy.
papers.journal: Journal of perianesthesia nursing : official journal of the American Society of PeriAnesthesia Nurses
papers.summary: In a single-center pilot of 68 pancreaticoduodenectomy patients, a nurse-delivered Omaha System-based perioperative pathway was associated with shorter time to first flatus, defecation, and ambulation and lower ISI and HADS scores on postoperative day 7 compared with routine care, with a non-significant lower complication proportion (5.88% vs 23.53%).

papers.title: A scoping review of nonpharmacologic strategies for use with Mediterranean youth with mixed chronic pain conditions: a culturally adapted approach.
papers.summary: This scoping review of 35 articles on nonpharmacologic interventions for Mediterranean youth with chronic pain found predominantly psychological/educational (n=18), physical (n=9), and dietary (n=7) strategies, and concluded that a comprehensive skill-based approach combining psychological strategies with healthy lifestyle recommendations may be culturally relevant.

papers.title: The symptom spectrum: preoperative symptom-related indicators of surgical outcomes for adult type 1 chiari malformation.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 209 adults with Chiari I malformation undergoing posterior fossa decompression, preoperative sleep apnea, imbalance, and tinnitus predicted 30-day symptom improvement, dysphagia predicted 90-day improvement, and hearing loss predicted long-term recurrence. Hand numbness/weakness and visual symptoms predicted lower odds of complete symptom resolution.

papers.title: Effects of six weeks of guanidinoacetic acid supplementation with and without creatine monohydrate on cognitive function and markers of health in healthy adults.
papers.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 58 healthy adults, six weeks of guanidinoacetic acid (GAA) supplementation with or without creatine monohydrate improved delayed verbal episodic recognition memory and some measures of perceived stress, sleep quality, and quality of life, but most cognitive tests were unaffected. No clinically meaningful changes in blood markers or side effects were observed.

papers.title: Behavioral and autonomic manifestations of suspected focal impaired awareness seizures supported by interictal electroencephalographic findings in three dogs: a case series.
papers.summary: This case series describes three dogs with suspected focal impaired awareness seizures presenting with behavioral and autonomic signs (fear, restlessness, hypersalivation) and epileptiform discharges on interictal EEG predominantly in parietal and temporal regions. Antiseizure medication reduced episode frequency and intensity, with complete seizure freedom in two dogs.

papers.title: A Standardized Nursing-Led Protocol Integrated Pain, Sleep, Medication Adherence, and Symptom Management in Postherpetic Neuralgia.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 128 adults with postherpetic neuralgia, an eight-week standardized nursing-led protocol integrating pain assessment, sleep monitoring, medication adherence, and digital symptom monitoring significantly reduced NRS pain scores (to 3.24 vs. 4.82 in usual care) and improved sleep quality, adherence, and symptom burden. The protocol group also had fewer breakthrough pain episodes and less rescue analgesic use.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
